minutes.headline: Selectmen renewed the town manager's contract at a higher salary and ratified two new police officers.
minutes.summary: The board approved a wine and malt license for a new Honey Farms store contingent on clean background checks, ratified two police appointments, and granted a one-day liquor license and a voluntary toll. It stayed the Mickey Shays suspension pending an ABCC appeal deadline, announced the town manager's renewed contract, and discussed financing options for the school building project debt.

what_happened.line: The Select Board announced a renewed town manager contract running three years, with a salary increase in each year, a December 1 deferred compensation payment and a performance bonus kept out of base pay.
The board voted to stay the Mickey Shays suspension if the ABCC appeal is confirmed as timely filed by noon the next day.
The board approved a wine and malt license for a new Honey Farms store, contingent on clean CORI checks for the owner and manager.
The board ratified two full-time police officer appointments, and approved a one-day liquor license and a Lions Club voluntary toll with police chief conditions.
The town manager was asked to investigate an interest-only or reduced-principal financing option for the school building project debt.

why_it_matters: The town manager contract sets pay and benefits for three years, which are paid from the town budget, mostly taxes.
How the school building debt is structured, including a 20- or 30-year bond, changes the total interest the town pays and the annual debt on tax bills.
watch_next: Whether the ABCC appeal on the Mickey Shays suspension was confirmed as timely filed by the noon deadline the day after the meeting.
The October 29 workshop on policies and procedures, and the town manager's report on the school project financing option.
